title: Why smells make us feel at home
speaker: BBC Learning English

keywords.def: unable to smell; having no sense of smell
quite a high likelihood or probability (that something will happen)
distinctive smell; smell produced by an animal
remove or separate something unwanted from a substance

sentences.en: Hello.
sentences.zh: 你好。

sentences.en: This is 6 Minute English from BBC Learning English.
sentences.zh: 这里是BBC英语教学的《6 Minute English》。

sentences.en: I’m Phil. And I’m Beth. Phil, what makes home special for you?
sentences.zh: 我是Phil。我是Beth。Phil，什么对你来说让家变得特别？

sentences.en: Maybe it’s sleeping in your own bed, the view from the window, or a loved family pet.
sentences.zh: 也许是睡在自己的床上、窗外的风景，或是心爱的宠物。

sentences.en: What makes you feel like you're home, Phil?
sentences.zh: 什么让你觉得你在家呢，Phil？

sentences.en: You know what? I think it's just relaxing on my sofa, in my living room.
sentences.zh: 你知道吗？我觉得就是在客厅的沙发上放松一下。

sentences.en: Very nice! Well, you may not realise it, but for your brain one of the strongest identifiers of home is smell.
sentences.zh: 非常好！嗯，你可能没有意识到，但对你的大脑来说，家的最强标识之一就是气味。

sentences.en: Listen as BBC presenters Marnie Chesterton and Tristan Ahtone describe the smells which give them the feeling of home: …My grandad's house smelt of pine and damp and musty books.
sentences.zh: 听听BBC主持人Marnie Chesterton和Tristan Ahtone描述带给他们归属感的气味：……我爷爷的房子里有松树、潮湿和发霉的书籍的气味。

sentences.en: …I know my mom's perfume, my dad’s preferred soap.
sentences.zh: ……我知道我妈妈的香水味，我爸爸最喜欢的肥皂味。

sentences.en: In this programme, we’ll be finding out why our sense of smell is so important to feeling at home, even when we don’t notice it.
sentences.zh: 在本期节目中，我们将探讨为什么嗅觉对于家的感觉如此重要，即使我们并没有注意到它。

sentences.en: As always, we’ll be introducing some useful new vocabulary, and if you head over to our website, bbclearningenglish.com, you’ll find a transcript of the programme to read along with as you listen, and there's a free worksheet too!
sentences.zh: 和往常一样，我们将介绍一些实用的新词汇。如果你访问我们的网站 bbclearningenglish.com，你会找到节目文稿，可以边听边读，还有一个免费的练习册！

sentences.en: Good idea, Beth! But now it’s time for my question.
sentences.zh: 好主意，Beth！但现在是时候提出我的问题了。

sentences.en: The sense of smell is incredibly powerful but not everyone has it.
sentences.zh: 嗅觉极其强大，但并非所有人都有嗅觉。

sentences.en: A small amount of the population is anosmic, meaning they can’t smell.
sentences.zh: 有一小部分人患有嗅觉缺失症，这意味着他们闻不到气味。

sentences.en: So, according to research at the University of Reading, what percentage of people have no sense of smell?
sentences.zh: 那么，根据雷丁大学的研究，有多少比例的人没有嗅觉？

sentences.en: Is it: a) 2%? b) 5%? or, c) 7%? Oh, I'm going to say b) 5%.
Well, we'll find out the correct answer later in the programme.
sentences.zh: 好的，我们将在节目后面揭晓正确答案。

sentences.en: Have you ever come back home from holiday and noticed a strange smell in your house?
sentences.zh: 你有没有过从度假回来后发现家里有一股奇怪气味的时候？

sentences.en: If you have, don’t worry – it’s not bad, in fact there’s a scientific reason for it, as science writer Tristan Ahtone explained to BBC World Service programme, Unexpected Elements:
sentences.zh: 如果有，别担心——这并不坏，事实上这背后有科学原因，正如科学作家Tristan Ahtone向BBC世界服务部节目《UnexpectedElements》解释的那样：

sentences.en: One thing I've been thinking about is that every house or home has, well, a smell to it.
sentences.zh: 我一直在思考的一点是，每座房子或每个家，嗯，都有它自己的气味。

sentences.en: You might really notice this in your own home when you come back from a long trip, and you step through your front door and things smell, well, just kind of a bit weird.
sentences.zh: 当你从漫长的旅行归来，走进前门，你会发现家里闻起来，嗯，有点怪怪的，这时你可能会真切地注意到这一点。

sentences.en: While there's a good chance your house might smell strange because it's been closed up for a few weeks, there's also a chance you might be smelling your home as it usually smells, but you just don't notice it when you're there.
sentences.zh: 虽然你的房子闻起来很奇怪很有可能是因为它已经关闭了几个星期，但也有可能是你闻到了它平时的气味，只是你在家的时候没有注意到而已。

sentences.en: Tristan says that when you return home after being away, there’s a good chance your house smells weird, an adjective meaning strange or unusual.
sentences.zh: Tristan说，当你离开一段时间后回到家，你的房子很有闻起来很奇怪的可能，“weird”这个形容词意思是奇怪或不寻常的。

sentences.en: If you say there’s a good chance that something will happen, you mean there’s a high likelihood or probability of it.
sentences.zh: 如果你说某事有很大的发生可能，意思就是它有很高的可能性或概率。

sentences.en: The truth is that every home has a smell, although we’re so used to it, we usually don’t notice.
sentences.zh: 事实是，每个家都有气味，尽管我们已经习以为常，通常不会注意到。

sentences.en: When we breathe in, receptor cells in the nose detect molecules in the air and send them to olfactory organs in the brain.
sentences.zh: 当我们吸气时，鼻子里的受体细胞探测到空气中的分子，并将它们发送到大脑的嗅觉器官。

sentences.en: These analyse the smells for danger. The reason you can't smell your own home is that it isn’t a threat to you.
sentences.zh: 这些器官会分析气味以寻找危险。你闻不到自己家的原因是因为它对你没有威胁。

sentences.en: Here’s science writer Tristan Ahtone again, explaining more to BBC World Service programme, Unexpected Elements:
sentences.zh: 再次听听科学作家Tristan Ahtone向BBC世界服务部节目《UnexpectedElements》做出的更多解释：

sentences.en: Well, by filtering out common non-threatening smells it makes it easier to detect things out of the ordinary that might be dangerous.
sentences.zh: 嗯，通过过滤掉常见的没有威胁的气味，可以让人更容易检测到可能存在危险的不寻常事物。

sentences.en: So, for example, if you forget about your toast, and it starts to burn, you can typically smell that quickly because it’s a change to the environment that you're in.
sentences.zh: 所以，举个例子，如果你把吐司忘了，它开始烧焦，你通常能很快闻到，因为这改变了你所处的环境。

sentences.en: Then the other parts of your brain kick in to understand the smell of smoke as a potential harm or threat.
sentences.zh: 然后你大脑的其他部分开始运转，将烟味理解为潜在的危害或威胁。

sentences.en: But even if we can't smell our own homes, the scent of them still matters because it's entangled with our recognition of comfort and security.
sentences.zh: 但即使我们闻不到自己家的气味，它的气味依然重要，因为它与我们对舒适和安全的认知交织在一起。

sentences.en: By filtering out familiar smells, our brains are able to detect other smells which are out of the ordinary, unusual or uncommon, and which may be dangerous.
sentences.zh: 通过过滤掉熟悉的气味，我们的大脑能够检测到其他不寻常、罕见或不常见、可能具有危险的气味。

sentences.en: To filter something out means to remove or separate something unwanted from something else.
sentences.zh: 过滤掉某物意味着将不需要的东西从其他东西中移除或分离出来。

sentences.en: For example, filtering out the smell of home means we notice the smell of burning toast or other smells alerting us to possible danger.
sentences.zh: 例如，过滤掉家的气味意味着我们能注意到烤吐司烧焦的气味或其他提醒我们注意潜在危险的气味。

sentences.en: Even though we don't usually notice the scent – the particular smell – of our home, it still has an effect on the brain's limbic system which handles memory and emotion.
sentences.zh: 尽管我们通常不会注意到家的气味——那种特定的气味——但它仍然对处理记忆和情绪的大脑边缘系统产生影响。

sentences.en: This explains why smell has such a strong effect on our feelings, and why we feel comfortable and safe at home.
sentences.zh: 这就解释了为什么气味对我们的情绪有如此强烈的影響，以及为什么我们在家里感到舒适和安全。

sentences.en: Right, Phil, isn’t it time to reveal the answer to your question?
sentences.zh: 对啦，Phil，是不是该揭晓你问题的答案了？

sentences.en: Yes, it is. I asked you what percentage of the population is anosmic, that means they can't smell.
sentences.zh: 是的，没错。我问你有多大比例的人口患有嗅觉缺失症，也就是他们闻不到气味。

sentences.en: And the answer is b) 5% which is what you said, I think.
sentences.zh: 答案是b) 5%，我想这也是你说的。

sentences.en: It is, yeah! Well done! OK, let’s recap the vocabulary we’ve learnt in this programme, starting with anosmic, meaning having no sense, or a limited sense, of smell.
sentences.zh: 是的，没错！干得好！好吧，让我们回顾一下我们在本节目中学到的词汇，首先是“anosmic”，意思是没有嗅觉或嗅觉有限。

sentences.en: The adjective weird means strange, odd or bizarre.
sentences.zh: 形容词“weird”意思是奇怪的、古怪的或离奇的。

sentences.en: When someone says there’s a good chance something will happen, they mean it’s quite likely to happen.
sentences.zh: 当某人说某事有很大可能发生时，意思是它很有可能会发生。

sentences.en: The phrase out of the ordinary means unusual, uncommon, or exceptional.
sentences.zh: 短语“out of the ordinary”意思是不同寻常的、罕见的或例外的。

sentences.en: If you filter something out, you remove or separate something unwanted from a substance.
sentences.zh: 如果你过滤掉某物，你就是从一种物质中移除或分离出不需要的东西。

sentences.en: And finally, a scent is a distinctive smell, often a pleasant one although it can also mean the smell made by an animal.
sentences.zh: 最后，“scent”是一种独特的香味，通常是令人愉悦的，尽管它也可以指动物产生的气味。

sentences.en: Once again, our six minutes are up, but if you enjoyed listening to this programme, you’ll find many more, along with a worksheet with a quiz you can try, on our website, bbclearningenglish.com.
sentences.zh: 我们的六分钟时间又到了，如果你喜欢听这个节目，你可以在我们的网站 bbclearningenglish.com 上找到更多节目以及包含测验的练习册。

sentences.en: See you there soon! Bye!
sentences.zh: 回见！再见！
